add_nodes.title: LISA launches
add_nodes.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
add_nodes.description: ESA's Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, three spacecraft 2.5 million km apart, launches toward its orbit around the Sun. It is the physical gate for all LISA science. The analysis stack can be ready years earlier, but no LISA data exist before this.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: Adopted by ESA in Jan 2024 (general); construction began Jun 17 2025, with launch planned for 2035 on Ariane 6 (ESA). NASA supplies telescopes, lasers and charge management; Congress funded NASA's share at $80.5M in FY2026 against a proposed cut, and ESA has prepared mitigation, including alternative telescope contracts (Wikipedia, LISA). China's Taiji and TianQin space detectors are proposed for about the same period (general).
add_nodes.why: Not an AI-math implication: an exogenous launch anchor that makes the physical clock visible in the LISA chain (science-lisa-precision-science needs it as a hard prerequisite). ESA's large science missions have usually launched one to three years after the date set at adoption (general), and the US share faces the FY2027 request's cuts. A launch inside 2035 therefore needs the plan to hold with no slip, so the node is Low in every scenario (judgment). AI mathematics and robots move integration and test by months at most. ESA budget phasing, the Ariane 6 manifest and the agency review cycle set the date, so the node is identical across scenarios, S4 included.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: ESA's large missions rarely launch on the date set at adoption, and a US withdrawal would force new telescope and laser contracts. Even an on-time launch gives first science only after about a year of transfer and commissioning.
add_nodes.signpost: LISA critical design review and the launch date in ESA's science programme updates; the enacted NASA LISA line each year.
add_nodes.note_2035: New in the 2035 extension: the planned launch sits at the edge of the horizon, so any slip pushes it past 2035. No scenario, S4 included, moves an agency launch date.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-science (2026-10-07): new node; exogenous launch anchor and hard prerequisite of science-lisa-precision-science.

add_nodes.title: Satellite methane numbers routinely correct reported emissions
add_nodes.pathway: P1->P5 (adoption into regulation; no hardware change)
add_nodes.description: Satellite emission-rate quantification with stated uncertainty becomes a standard verification input under at least one major regime: EU Methane Regulation operator reporting, importer equivalence or methane-intensity checks; a national regulator's penalty or super-emitter program; or national inventory review under the Paris transparency framework. Measurable test: at least 100 facility-level corrections a year, or a national inventory revision, rest on satellite numbers with their uncertainties.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: Satellites trigger notifications but do not yet set numbers: UNEP IMEO's MARS sends plumes to governments and operators (European Commission). EU 2024/1787 phases in importer duties from 2027 and methane-intensity limits from 2030 (dates general). Supply is growing: Tanager-1 (2024) and GHGSat's satellites operate, and the Copernicus CO2M constellation is due from about 2027 (general); MethaneSAT was lost in Jun 2025 (Wikipedia).
add_nodes.why: The step after first use (science-eo-ghg-enforcement-grade): one accepted case becomes a standard method. Chain (S2): first compliance use 2030 -> verifier methodologies and early disputes settle 2031-32 -> routine use under the EU intensity regime 2033. S3 is a year earlier through its earlier first use. Each step needs regulator acceptance and politics does not compress, so the node sits a band below first use: S3 Medium and S2 Low by 2035, S1 after 2035 (Speculative). No hardware step: existing and planned constellations suffice. Robots add nothing, so S4 equals S3. Bands are judgments.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Regulators may keep satellites as screening tools and rely on operator reports and aerial surveys, which are easier to defend. The EU importer regime has faced pressure to relax for LNG suppliers (general), and orbital imagers see only large plumes, so most small leaks stay invisible from space (general).
add_nodes.signpost: An EU or member-state verification report in which satellite quantification sets or corrects reported volumes; the methane-intensity methodology naming top-down measurement; a national inventory revised on satellite evidence.
add_nodes.note_2035: New in the 2035 extension: the Earth-observation chain reaches routine use inside the horizon in S2-S4. Regulators and politics set the pace, so S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-science (2026-10-07): new node extending the Earth-observation chain past science-eo-ghg-enforcement-grade.

add_nodes.title: A 1,000-planet atmosphere census with honest error bars
add_nodes.description: ESA's ARIEL, or another survey of hundreds of exoplanet atmospheres, publishes population results with per-planet identifiability statements: which molecules and temperature structures each spectrum determines and which it cannot. Population trends (metallicity, carbon-to-oxygen ratio, clouds) then rest on stated, comparable uncertainties.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: ARIEL was adopted by ESA in Nov 2020 for a 2029 launch on Ariane 6 and plans to observe about 1,000 transiting planets over four years (general). JWST retrievals of the same spectrum still give 'parallel interpretations' (PNAS, Sep 2025).
add_nodes.why: The first large, uniform exoplanet spectral survey is where identifiability theory (science-retrieval-identifiability, S2 2028) becomes standard practice for a whole dataset. Chain: launch 2029 -> commissioning and a first pass of the target list over about two years -> population papers 2033. Photons set the date, so the node is identical across scenarios; AI shortens the analysis by months. Medium by 2035 in every scenario because ESA missions often slip a year or two (general) and population results need most of the first survey pass. No S4 credit: the spacecraft is built before robots do aerospace work, and the survey clock is orbital.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: ARIEL's spectra have lower resolution than JWST's, so many retrievals will be degenerate whatever the theory. Identifiability statements may mostly list what cannot be known.
add_nodes.signpost: ARIEL launch date and first survey data release; consortium population papers reporting identifiability maps per target.
add_nodes.note_2035: New in the 2035 extension: ARIEL's survey data arrive in 2031-33, so the exoplanet chain reaches a population result inside the horizon. Photons bind, so S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-science (2026-10-07): new node extending the exoplanet retrieval chain past science-retrieval-identifiability.

add_nodes.title: Science missions designed to send answers, not raw data
add_nodes.description: A science mission selected after 2028 puts onboard science products with certified error bounds into its requirements, so its downlink and ground segment are sized for answers. Raw data become the exception, kept for calibration and audits. A constellation, an Explorer-class or larger mission, or a deep-space probe counts.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: No science mission is designed this way. Onboard autonomy flies as an add-on (EO-1 from 2004 and AEGIS on Mars rovers, general; Phi-sat-2 since 2024, ESA), and requirements still assume raw or losslessly compressed downlink (general).
add_nodes.why: Second-generation step after the first mission accepts onboard products (science-onboard-science-inference, S2 2029). Chain (S2): first accepted use 2029 -> a proposal team baselines it for a 2029-30 opportunity -> selection 2030 -> build and launch about 2033 at smallsat or Explorer cadence. S3 is 2032 through an earlier, more confident start; S1 2035. Downlink is the domain's main data-supply limit, and deep-space links gain most. Medium by 2035 in S2-S4 because selections are scarce under the FY2027 request and review boards are wary of discarding raw data; S1 Low. No S4 credit: selection and launch bind.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Optical links may raise downlink faster than onboard inference saves it, and science teams prize raw data for re-analysis, so missions may keep raw downlink as the baseline.
add_nodes.signpost: An Explorer, Discovery, ESA M-class or commercial science proposal with onboard products in its top-level requirements; a smallsat science constellation that tasks itself from onboard products.
add_nodes.note_2035: New in the 2035 extension: missions selected around 2030 launch in 2032-35 with onboard products designed in. Selection binds, so S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-science (2026-10-07): new node extending the onboard-inference chain past science-onboard-science-inference.

add_nodes.title: A Sun-watching constellation designed for 3D reconstruction flies
add_nodes.description: A multi-spacecraft heliophysics or space-weather mission (smallsats at several viewpoints, or L4/L5 plus polar) whose number, placement and instruments were chosen by reconstruction-uniqueness analysis launches and returns 3D coronal or solar-wind reconstructions with stated uncertainty.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: Multi-point missions fly or are planned with conventional trades: PUNCH (four smallsats, launched 2025), HelioSwarm (nine spacecraft, planned for about 2029) and ESA's Vigil at L5 (about 2031) (general). No mission concept is yet justified by reconstruction-uniqueness analysis (general).
add_nodes.why: Flight step after the design method (science-helio-constellation-design, S2 2029). Chain (S2): concept studies 2029-30 -> selection in a 2030-31 Explorer, partner or operational opportunity -> four to five years to launch, about 2035. S3 is a year earlier through faster proposal and design closure; capital and selection still bind. Low by 2035 in S2-S4 because Explorer slots are scarce under the FY2027 request and a constellation needs one of them or a new operational space-weather budget; S1 after 2035 (Speculative). No S4 credit: selection and budgets bind, and smallsat integration is not the slow step.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Constellations are chosen by launch slots, partner contributions and budgets. Uniqueness analysis may only confirm designs that heritage would have chosen anyway.
add_nodes.signpost: A heliophysics Explorer or ESA mission selection whose proposal cites reconstruction-uniqueness analysis; a NOAA or ESA operational space-weather constellation designed the same way.
add_nodes.note_2035: New in the 2035 extension: a constellation selected around 2030-31 could fly by 2034-35, at the edge of the horizon. Selection and budgets bind, so S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-science (2026-10-07): new node extending the heliophysics chain past science-helio-constellation-design.

patch.thesis: Base case: AI doubles archival science per dollar from 2028 and readies LISA's analysis around 2031, well before launch. Satellite methane numbers become compliance evidence around 2030. LISA still launches in 2035 at the earliest. S4 adds no year: photons, budgets, regulators and launch dates set the pace.
